account:
Today’s business has involved an unusual amount of appointment clarification. The secretary had a second appointment book, which initially made me wonder whether arrangements were being made without me. She explains that it was a provisional record made before she received the original, and that the original remains authoritative. I saw her take a written book from the appointments chest this morning. She says written confirmation of tea is now in that chest. Neighbour personally confirmed that I am expected at the east-bank cottage at three today; the secretary also confirms tea there tomorrow. On present evidence, this looks like scheduling confusion rather than proof of a secret arrangement.

Builder has repeatedly requested a meeting tomorrow at eighteen hundred in the great hall, with the secretary accompanying me. He says eight lanterns have been installed around the four tables and wants us to check that the lighting is even and comfortable. I have agreed and asked the secretary to record it. The repeated confirmations are noticeable, but I have no evidence that the meeting is for anything other than the stated inspection.

Two residents reported seeing baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn. That could be an ordinary delivery; I have not seen it myself or learned its purpose. The town accounts appointment has meanwhile produced no accounts papers: the secretary says she has not received them, and I do not know where they are. I intend to check the treasury before leaving for tea. I still feel somewhat out of touch with town activity, but none of these observations yet establishes that people are concealing anything from me.
